gap: No result ChatGPT got states that two leading solar cameras rate battery life on the same 300-seconds-of-recording-a-day basis (eufy SoloCam S340 about 3 months, Reolink Argus 4 Pro about 2 months), or that the S340's built-in panel is only 2.2 W, below the 5–10 W ChatGPT itself recommends, so eufy relies on 2 hours of direct sun a day rather than panel size.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran an empty search in both saved chats (no results, no citations, no product cards), so there are no rival pages to compare against. Its own answer gives generic advice ('Solar panel 5–10W or more', 'Battery sized for several cloudy days'). It names no product's panel wattage, battery-life basis, sun-hours requirement or 24/7 limitation, so a normalised table is new. It doesn't reach 3 because I couldn't get battery capacities on a common Wh basis (eufy publishes no mAh; Reolink gives no voltage) or Arenti's specs.
decides: It confirms rather than flips the pick. On the makers' shared 300 s/day basis the eufy S340 claims 3 months to Reolink Argus 4 Pro's 2 months. But its 2.2 W built-in panel is under ChatGPT's own 5–10 W guideline, and eufy itself says it needs 2 hours of direct sun daily. The Argus 4 Pro uses Reolink's separate 6 W Solar Panel 2, which suits shaded or northern sites better. Mighty Gadget measured the Argus 4 Pro at about 25% left after about 3 weeks on battery alone, worse than Reolink's 2-month claim, so the panel matters. Neither line supports 24/7 recording on battery (eufy says so explicitly; Reolink lists only triggered recording).
